title: Relight a gas water heater's pilot: hold the knob in while the other hand sparks, until the status light blinks
instruction: The gas is back on after a repair. Light the water heater and leave it set to HOT.
context: Plumbers (O*NET 47-2152.00, 510,600 workers) list 'Install pipe assemblies, fittings, valves, appliances such as dishwashers or water heaters'; a standing-pilot heater is lit at the end of every install, and pilots are relit after every gas shutoff, also by general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00, 1,621,800) in apartment buildings. The maker's label: knob to PILOT, press it in about 1/4 in and hold, click the igniter about once a second 'for up to 90 seconds or until Status Light begins to blink', then release and set the temperature. Unlike a momentary button press, one hand must keep about 15 N on a 29 mm knob for 40 s or more, all the way in, while the other snaps a stiff button 40 mm below it on the same upright face. The status light, not a stop, says when to let go: too early and the pilot goes out and the control locks out for 10 minutes.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases at (0, 30.5) and (0, -30.5); positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table, which stands for the floor. Water heater: the lower front of a 40 gal atmospheric natural-gas heater (A.O. Smith GCR-40 size), fixed: a 116-degree arc of its 50.8 cm (20 in) painted-steel jacket, 56 cm tall, centred on y 0, its front at x 40.6. Burner opening (outer door off): 16 cm wide, 3.5 to 21.5 cm up; recessed in it the dark steel inner door with a 2.6 x 2.0 cm sight glass 11 cm up, the pilot burner and thermopile behind it. Gas control, modelled on the Resideo (Honeywell) WV8840B (trade WT8840B1000), fixed on the jacket, back 0.5 cm off it: grey plastic cover 13.5 wide x 13.3 tall x 8.1 cm deep, face at x 32.0, from y -6.0 to 7.6 and 26.6 to 39.9 cm up. Knob: red plastic, 2.9 cm across, 1.6 cm proud, with a 0.5 x 2.6 cm grip ridge; axis at y 5.0, 32.25 cm up; marks clockwise from OFF: PILOT 30, VAC 60, LOW 92, HOT (120 F) 122, A 155, B 182, C 206, VERY HOT 244 degrees; at PILOT only it pushes in 6.35 mm against a spring (about 6 N at first, 15.5 N fully in: estimates); pushed in, it does not turn. Piezo igniter: red plastic square button 1.1 cm, 0.7 cm proud in a 1.5 cm bezel, 4.0 cm below the knob's axis (y 4.75, 28.25 cm up), pushed straight in, 5 mm travel, 8 N to start, 20 N at the 4 mm snap (estimates). Status light: 4.5 mm red lens, 7.8 cm right of the knob, 1.45 cm above its axis. Gas supply: 1/2 in black-iron pipe from the control's left-side inlet (31.1 cm up) to a tee at y 18 with a capped drip leg, and a riser with a brass quarter-turn shutoff valve, yellow handle, open. Start: knob at OFF (the label's 10-minute wait at OFF is over), pilot out, status light dark. Distractors (scoring ignores them): an adjustable wrench, steel, 21 x 6.4 x 1.4 cm, 300 g, at (20, 27), turned -20 degrees; 10 in groove-joint pliers, steel with green grips, 24.6 x 6.5 x 1.4 cm, 280 g, at (52, -42), turned 70 degrees; a cotton cleaning cloth, 26 x 23.3 x 2.1 cm, 50 g, at (55, 42), turned 10 degrees.
scoring: Kept for the whole trial and cleared only by a reset: if pilot gas flows with no flame for more than 90 s in total (the knob held in at PILOT with the pilot out; the label's limit for one attempt), the score is 0. Otherwise: 1.0 when the pilot is lit and held by the control (status light blinking), the knob let out (in less than 1 mm), the knob within 8 degrees of the HOT mark, and every fingertip at least 3 cm from the knob and the igniter, all for 5 s in a row; the trial ends there. Else, at the end: 0.5 if the pilot is lit and held by the control and the knob is let out, at HOT + 8 degrees or cooler (PILOT, VAC, LOW, or HOT with a hand still on it or for less than 5 s); 0.25 if the pilot was lit at some point but now is out (let out before the light blinked, or turned to OFF), is still being held in, or is set more than 8 degrees past HOT (toward A to VERY HOT, a scald risk); 0 if it never lit. The pilot: a spark lights it only while the knob is in at least 5.5 mm at PILOT; the control holds it after 40 s of flame; let out sooner, it goes out and the control will not hold again for 10 minutes. Real trial: the light blinking once every 3 s and the flame through the sight glass (a camera at the burner opening); the knob's angle from a photo of the dial; the push-in, the unlit time and fingertip clearance from the video.
reset_notes: Between real trials, turn the knob to OFF, close the shutoff valve and wait 10 minutes (the label's wait between lighting attempts; the status light goes out first). In simulation a reset restores the knob to OFF and the pilot out.
fidelity: The flame, spark and thermopile are bookkeeping, not combustion: a spark lights the pilot only with the knob in 5.5 mm or more at PILOT; the control holds it after 40 s of flame. No gas, heat or CO is simulated. Knob, push-in and igniter are sprung joints with estimated forces. Control, jacket, door and pipes are rigid primitives at real size (the control's scaled from the makers' figures); label text is drawn as lines. Tools and cloth: SimReady props. Uniform high friction; no force sensing.
